items.title: B688's quick-fix for an impl block in a USER module steers to the module's first exported declaration (`import pkg::styles::search_mark_style;` to reach `impl Style { fun ghost }`), which reads as an unrelated import: a selector-only import of the block would be the honest steer
items.discussion: lane solver-56 (post-Order 55): B688's rule admits a block through any import whose path runs through its file (visibility.md §3.2) or a selector-only import; the quick-fix picks the file's first export as the name to import, so kolt's 86 sites get steers like `import pkg::styles::search_mark_style;` for a style helper the file never calls
items.body: The import the rule WANTS is 'this file reaches `pkg::styles`', not that name; the steer should spell the reach - a selector-only import of the block (`import pkg::styles::{ (impl Style) }` if that form exists, else the module itself) - and name the block in the sentence. Rec: the smallest honest spelling the grammar has today; if none, say in the message that any name from the module serves and pick a declaration the block's type mentions. Sizing S.
